glory] I.e. effulgence of light (see OED 6).
 Locock 1911 cps Athanase Detached Passage (b) l. 14.
 Cp. the snow on tree-branches reflecting moonlight in Coleridge, Frost at Midnight ll. 68–74.
 rime] I.e. hoar-frost.
 it] Written above he canc. in Nbk 16.
 its] Altered from his in Nbk 16.
 the torrent of the night] The sense is of a night sky’s rushing stream of light (see OED 2b).
 Breasting] Breathing BSM (reading of Nbk 16), MT. I.e. ‘opposing the breast to’ (OED 1), as in
Henry V, III. Prol. 13 ‘Breasting the lofty surge.’
 Or . . . Or] I.e. ‘Either . . . or’. The lines refer to a night sky unilluminated by the moon. On the
‘inchanted’ associations of ‘a waning moon’, see Coleridge, Kubla Khan ll. 14–15.
 the noon of interlunar night] ‘The time of night corresponding to midday: midnight’ (OED).
 ‘Interlunar’ means between a waning and a waxing moon (see PU II iv 91 and note).
